title: BBB Security for the Nonce–Counter-Sum Mode
summary: Nonce-respecting use still permits easy tweak-input collisions, and whether the proposed mode attains beyond-birthday-bound security remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Consider the authenticated-encryption mode that places the sum of the nonce and counter in the tweak input and the IV in the plaintext input. Determine whether this mode achieves beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security in the nonce-respecting setting. The unresolved obstacle is that, even when nonces are respected, an adversary can readily induce collisions among tweak inputs, potentially complicating a BBB-security proof.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption mode design using tweakable block ciphers.
parameters: Nonce and counter: their sum is placed in the tweak input
IV: placed in the plaintext input
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the mode achieves beyond-birthday-bound security in the nonce-respecting setting despite adversarial tweak-input collisions.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the mode as potentially meeting its security objectives but leaves beyond-birthday-bound security unsettled. It identifies easily induced tweak-input collisions under respected nonces as a potential proof complication.
citation_labels: Thomas Peyrin et al., Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers
